messages:
alice_sdk: FYI I hit a pretty nasty bug in the async Python SDK when using it as a context manager together with asyncio timeouts — leads to request replay / duplicate side effects (e.g. duplicate DB row). Minimal repro in a sample app below.

alice_sdk: repro:
```py
# sample_app.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    # using a short timeout to hit transient 5xx during testing
    async with AsyncClient(api_key="x") as client:
        try:
            # server returns 502 briefly -> transport timeout -> client retries
            await client.create_completion(model="x", prompt="do thing")
        except Exception as e:
            print('caught', e)

asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(main(), timeout=3))
```

alice_sdk: observed behavior: client raises TimeoutError to caller, but server actually processed the request and our retry policy re-sent it once, so the side effect happened twice.

ben_infra: can you paste the client logs and the raw request id? does this happen only with asyncio.wait_for or also with AsyncClient(timeout=)?

alice_sdk: logs (sanitized):
```
2026-02-14T10:01:12.345Z DEBUG sending request id=req-abc body=POST /v1/completions
2026-02-14T10:01:14.999Z WARN transport timeout during send id=req-abc
2026-02-14T10:01:15.001Z ERROR context manager __aexit__ closing client with inflight send id=req-abc
2026-02-14T10:01:15.100Z INFO retrying request id=req-abc -> new-id=req-abc-retry1
2026-02-14T10:01:15.200Z INFO request succeeded id=req-abc-retry1
```

alice_sdk: so caller saw the TimeoutError from wait_for, but the SDK retried right after even though the original send might have actually reached the server.

charlie_oncall: we saw similar during a spike last month — when transport-level write hangs and user cancels the parent task, __aexit__ doesn't guarantee the underlying send is cancelled at the socket layer. The SDK's retry policy treats a send timeout as transient and replays immediately.

charlie_oncall: quick workaround: generate and attach an idempotency key in your app for non-idempotent endpoints. or explicitly await client.aclose() before letting the outer timeout kill the task.

ben_infra: thanks. Sounds like two issues: (1) context manager/close doesn't wait for inflight send cancellation to complete, (2) retry policy should be more conservative when the caller cancels/closes. We should avoid replaying when the cancellation is ambiguous.

ben_infra: suggested fix: mark the request as "uncertain" on transport timeout and defer automatic replay until a confirmation check (e.g. GET /status or server-sent request-id ack), or require idempotency for mutating endpoints. Alternatively, make the default backoff longer in cancellation cases so we reduce probability of double-apply.

alice_sdk: I opened an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4523 — includes the sample app and logs. Will try a quick PR for client close behavior.

devex-bot: Issue #4523 created by alice_sdk: "async context/timeout -> potential replay of POSTs; duplicate side effects". Labels: bug, sdk-python, high-priority.

ben_infra: proposed patch sketch (pseudo):
```py
# in transport.py
async def _send_with_guard(request):
    try:
        await transport.send(request)  # this is the socket write/stream send
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        # caller canceled — do NOT auto-retry immediately; surface as CancelledError
        raise
    except TransportTimeoutError as e:
        # mark as uncertain and raise a special UncertainSendError
        raise UncertainSendError(original=e)

# retry policy: if UncertainSendError -> do not auto-retry unless idempotency_key present
```

charlie_oncall: +1 add a unit test that simulates server processing after client timeout (use a fake server that delays ack after receiving bytes). Also add an integration test to ensure we don't double-write without explicit idempotency.

alice_sdk: will draft PR that: (a) makes __aexit__ wait for internal send tasks to either finish or be deterministically cancelled, (b) surfaces UncertainSendError, (c) updates retry policy to skip auto-retry when uncertain unless idempotency_key is set.

ben_infra: thanks — also update docs / migration note. We'll need a short-term patch for customers: recommend adding idempotency keys and bumping retry backoff if you rely on asyncio.wait_for.

alice_sdk: thanks all. I'll post the PR link here when ready. cc @charlie_oncall for test ideas.

charlie_oncall: great — if you want I can attach the incident trace from the spike so you can reproduce the same timing.

alice_sdk: that would be super helpful. thanks :pray:
